number_of_offences: Two offences/counts were charged, and both were finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The enquiry officer observed that the evidence on record does not substantiate the charge of demand and acceptance of bribe by the accused.
trial_duration: The trial judgment was dated 25.8.2008, and the Supreme Court decision was on 31 August 2012.
legal_representation: For the appellant: J.S. Attry, Anjani Aiyagari, Gargi Khanna, B.V. Bairam Das. For the respondent: Chelan Sharma, Bake Bihari Sharma (for Asha Gopalan Nair).
investigation_status: Charge-sheet filed on 19th September 2002, trial completed, disciplinary proceedings kept in abeyance due to pendency of criminal case.
appeal_history: Trial court: The accused filed a writ petition before the High Court, which was dismissed. High Court: The High Court quashed the criminal proceedings. Supreme Court: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court order, and directed the departmental proceedings to be reopened.
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the High Court's order to quash the criminal proceedings was based on an erroneous premise, as the accused had not been exonerated in the departmental proceedings, and that the disciplinary authority's exonerating order was conditional and dependent on the outcome of the criminal case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused had been exonerated in the departmental proceedings and that the criminal proceedings should be quashed on that ground alone, relying on the precedent set in P.S. Rajya v. State of Bihar.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that exoneration in departmental proceedings does not ipso facto lead to the quashing of criminal prosecution, and that the standard of proof in departmental proceedings is lower than that in criminal cases.
precedent_relied_upon: State v. M. Krishna Mohan (2007) 14 SCC 667; Supdt. of Police (C.B.I.) v. Deepak Chowdhary (1995) 6 SCC 225; Central Bureau of Investigation v. V.K. Bhutiani (2009) 10 SCC 674; P.S. Rajya v. State of Bihar 1996 (9) SCC 1
